title: Compact frame protocol for tool calls and offline retry (PRD draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD for a lightweight framing protocol and SDK ergonomics that target low-latency streaming with robust tool-calling and offline-retry semantics. The goal is to give client apps a compact, predictable wire format that makes it easy to route partial results to UI, call external tools deterministically, and recover cleanly if connectivity or backend tiers fail.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Current streaming designs mix large JSON blobs, ad-hoc partial messages, and client-side parsing rules. That complexity makes tool-handshakes brittle and increases chances of duplicate tool invocations during reconnects.
- Mobile and embedded clients require minimal on-wire payloads and a deterministic reconnection model (resume tokens, idempotent tool calls).
- We need an SDK-facing surface that is simple for common sync/async patterns but powerful enough to hook into structured-output validations, function/tool calling, and fallback model variants.

Goals (high level):
- Define a compact frame envelope suitable for binary and text transports (small header + typed payload).
- Specify deterministic tool-call lifecycle: handshake, acceptance, execution id, finalization, and idempotency tokens.
- Support resumable streams with resume cursors, duplicate-suppression hints, and optional offline retry semantics for non-idempotent tool calls.
- Provide a small SDK contract (JS/Python) that exposes simple sync/async APIs and clear error modes (transient, permanent, recovered).
- Make structured output (schemas) first-class in frames so caller can validate incrementally.

Non-goals:
- Not a full RPC layer (no transport-level guarantees beyond best-effort resume + id tokens).
- Not replacing existing complex orchestration flows for large enterprise private deployments—this focuses on Hosted API SDK ergonomics and core protocol primitives.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Frame: minimal envelope that wraps a typed payload (header fields below).
- Frame types: CHUNK, TOOL_OFFER, TOOL_ACCEPT, TOOL_RESULT, SCHEMA_META, RESUME_CURSOR, HEARTBEAT, ERROR, FINAL.
- Execution ID: opaque id assigned by server for each accepted tool invocation.
- Idempotency token: client-provided token (or server-generated) used to suppress duplicates across reconnects/retries.
- Resume cursor: opaque cursor pointing to stream position (used to request only subsequent frames).

Frame format (compact):
- Versioned header (fixed 1 byte): protocol version.
- Type (1 byte): enum of frame types.
- Flags (1 byte): bitflags for partial/final/urgent.
- Payload length (varint): bytes in payload.
- Payload (binary): CBOR preferred for compactness; JSON allowed for debug-only transports.
- Optional metadata trailer (varint length + key-value pairs) for routing hints.

Why CBOR: compactness + well-known libraries across platforms, binary-safe, supports schema pointers. We'll keep JSON option for developer-mode endpoints.

Tool-call lifecycle (example):
- Client sends TOOL_OFFER frame with: tool-name, version, call-params (CBOR map), optional idempotency_token.
- Server validates and responds with TOOL_ACCEPT with execution_id and expected cost/timeout or TOOL_REJECT with reject_reason.
- When accepted, client or server can stream CHUNK frames (partial textual content or structured frames) tagged with execution_id.
- On completion server emits TOOL_RESULT with execution_id + result_payload and FINAL.

Offline retry model (principles):
- Idempotent calls: client can safely retry with same idempotency token; server will return previous TOOL_ACCEPT/TOOL_RESULT if execution already completed.
- Non-idempotent calls: SDK warns and can request a delayed-offline-buffer mode where the client buffers tool offers locally and only flushes when back online. Server will reject replay attempts without explicit force flag.
- Reconnect flow: client resends last known resume cursor in RESUME_CURSOR frame. Server returns missing frames since cursor. If a TOOL_ACCEPT/TOOL_RESULT for an execution_id is already delivered, the server will include it and set a DUPLICATE flag in header to help client suppress double-processing.

Structured output and incremental validation:
- SCHEMA_META frames contain a compact schema id (pointer to registered schema) and optional sample.
- CHUNK frames can include typed fragments that validate against the SCHEMA_META. SDK exposes incremental validation hooks: onFragmentValidated, onSchemaMismatch.
- Tool outputs are strongly typed by default. Unstructured text remains allowed under a TEXT chunk type.

SDK ergonomics proposal (JS + Python):
- Minimal public surface: createStream(requestOpts) -> StreamHandle.
- StreamHandle methods: on('chunk', cb), on('tool_offer', cb), callTool(name, params, opts) -> Promise/awaitable ToolHandle, resume(cursor) -> Promise, close() -> Promise.
- ToolHandle: status, execution_id, result() -> Promise, cancel() -> Promise, on('progress', cb).
- Synchronous helpers: streamToCompletion(req) -> returns aggregated structured result (for sync use-cases).
- Mobile pattern: startLocalBuffering(opts) - buffer tool_offers locally; flushBufferedOffers() when connectivity restored.

Examples (JS pseudocode):
- Accepting a tool offer automatically:
  const s = createStream({model: 'rwi-compact-1'});
  s.on('tool_offer', async (offer) => {
    if (shouldAccept(offer)) {
      const th = await s.callTool(offer.name, offer.params, {idempotency: generateId()});
      th.on('progress', p => ui.update(p));
      const r = await th.result();
      // attach to conversation
    } else {
      // send decline frame (opt)
    }
  });

Rollout and compatibility:
- Versioning: header 1 byte ensures forward/backward compatibility. We'll ship version 1 as opt-in transport on the Hosted API (HTTP/2 + WebSocket endpoints).
- Fallback: the existing JSON SSE/streaming path remains unchanged; gateways will translate between full JSON frames and compact frames where possible.
- SDKs will default to the compact frame transport when platform supports CBOR; otherwise fallback to JSON.

Success metrics (initial):
- Developer adoption: 30% of new Streaming SDK integrations use compact frames in first quarter after launch.
- Latency: 20% reduction in median per-chunk wire payload size for mobile clients.
- Safety: 0 reconnection-related duplicate tool executions for idempotent flows in alpha test.
- Error clarity: Reduction in 'unknown' tool-state support tickets by 40% (tracked via CS triage).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- CBOR vs MessagePack: CBOR preferred but evaluate lib maturity on older Android versions.
- How aggressive should server be in deduplication for non-idempotent calls if client omitted tokens? Risk of silent replay vs forced rejections.
- Resume cursor exposure: how opaque should it be? (Opaque is safer; human debuggability suffers.)
- Schema registry: should schemas be globally versioned in product or scoped per-customer?

Next steps / action items:
- Eng (Marco) to prototype header parsing + varint payloads for HTTP/2 DATA frames (2 weeks).
- SDK (Diego) to sketch JS/Python small API surface and sample app using mobile-local-buffering pattern (2 weeks).
- Security & Compliance (Priya) to review replay/idempotency risk and propose KMS-backed id token options (1 week).
- Product to prepare a short alpha with 3 pilot customers and internal apps (post-prototype).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact and pragmatic; we prefer small increments (header + CBOR first) then add schema registry and richer server-side replay heuristics.
- Looking for feedback on: resume token shape, idempotency token lifecycle, and preferred SDK call patterns for mobile devs.
